about: Blind-read questions. 'needs' is 'structure' when the answer takes following arcs across several nodes or playing the net out, 'label' when one printed label or one arc answers it. 'derived' says how the answer was obtained: probe.ts is `npx tsx ../prototype/notation/corpus/probe.ts <file>` from studio/, engine.ts is the verify skill's summary. A moment is named by its marked states.

duel-first.maps.question: At the start, who acts first, Link or the enemy?
duel-first.maps.answer: Link. The world is silent at the start, so only Link can speak: hold, strike, raise the shield, or roll.
duel-first.maps.derived: probe.ts: the root moment (neutral, idle) is a seat turn for link. Every world verb takes or needs beat, ebeat, after, attack, striking, or recover, and none is marked at the start.

duel-first.maps.question: While the enemy winds up and Link stands ready, what can Link do, and what happens after each?
duel-first.maps.answer: Hold: the swing hits Link. Strike: the strike breaks the wind-up and Link lands a hit. Raise the shield: the shield stops the blow and the enemy reels into recovery, with Link still behind the shield. Roll: the blow whiffs over the roll and the enemy is left recovering, with Link standing ready.
duel-first.maps.derived: probe.ts moment (neutral, windup): wait > tick, swing, hit; strike > interrupt; guard > tick, swing, block, end to (guarding, recover); roll > tick, swing, evade, rollend to (neutral, recover). Each at odds 1.

duel-first.maps.question: Where are the windows in which a strike lands?
duel-first.maps.answer: Two. While the enemy winds up (the strike breaks the wind-up), and while the enemy is recovering (the strike lands in the opening). Link can strike into both from standing ready or from behind the shield.
duel-first.maps.derived: Arcs: interrupt takes windup and needs striking; punish takes recover and needs striking; both give enemy_hit. probe.ts: strike or guard_strike leads to 'Link lands a hit' at (neutral, windup), (guarding, windup), (neutral, recover), (guarding, recover).

duel-first.maps.question: How does the enemy end up recovering?
duel-first.maps.answer: Either Link blocks its swing with the shield or Link rolls under it. Both leave the enemy recovering for one beat, then it steadies back to idle.
duel-first.maps.derived: Arcs: block and evade both take attack and give recover; steady takes recover and ebeat and gives idle.

duel-first.maps.question: When is it unsafe to be behind the shield?
duel-first.maps.answer: It never is while the shield stays up: a swing at Link behind the shield is always blocked. Lowering the shield while the enemy winds up gets Link hit.
duel-first.maps.derived: probe.ts moment (guarding, windup): wait > block; lower > tick, swing, hit. hit needs neutral, block needs guarding.

duel-first.maps.question: Is there a move that wins outright whenever the enemy winds up?
duel-first.maps.answer: Yes. Striking (from ready or from the shield) during any wind-up ends the duel with Link landing a hit, at odds 1.
duel-first.maps.derived: probe.ts: every moment with windup marked offers strike or guard_strike, and each leads to interrupt at odds 1.

duel-first.maps.question: Can the duel go on forever?
duel-first.maps.answer: Yes. Link can keep the shield up and keep blocking, and the duel never ends. The analysis counts plays as endless.
duel-first.maps.derived: engine.ts: plays 'endless'. probe.ts cycle (guarding, idle) > wait > (guarding, windup) > wait > (guarding, recover) > wait > (guarding, idle).

duel-first.maps.question: How many distinct resting moments does this duel have, where Link must decide?
What can Link do from behind the shield that needs no lowering first?
duel-first.maps.derived: Arcs: guard_strike takes guarding and gives striking and beat.

duel-revised.maps.question: While the enemy winds up and Link stands ready, what can Link do, and what happens after each?
duel-revised.maps.answer: Hold: the swing hits Link. Strike: the strike finishes and then the swing hits Link. Raise the shield: the shield stops the blow and pushes Link back, and the enemy returns to idle. Roll: the blow whiffs over the roll and the enemy is left recovering.
duel-revised.maps.derived: probe.ts moment (neutral, windup): wait and strike lead to hit; guard to (guarding, idle); roll to (neutral, recover).

duel-revised.maps.question: Where is the punish window?
duel-revised.maps.answer: Only while the enemy recovers from a whiffed swing, after Link rolls under it. Striking then lands a hit.
duel-revised.maps.derived: Arcs: punish takes recover and needs striking; only evade gives recover (block gives idle). probe.ts: (neutral, recover) strike > punish.

duel-revised.maps.question: From the start, what is the shortest way to land a hit?
duel-revised.maps.answer: Three choices: anything but raising the shield (the enemy winds up), then roll (the swing whiffs), then strike (the strike lands in the opening).
duel-revised.maps.derived: probe.ts: root (neutral, idle) > wait, strike, or roll > (neutral, windup) > roll > (neutral, recover) > strike > punish. No other moment reaches enemy_hit in one choice.

duel-revised.maps.question: Is striking while the enemy winds up ever a good idea?
duel-revised.maps.answer: No. It always ends with Link taking a hit.
duel-revised.maps.derived: probe.ts (neutral, windup) strike > whiff, tick, swing, hit at odds 1. There is no verb that takes windup and needs striking.

duel-revised.maps.question: Can Link strike without first standing ready?
duel-revised.maps.answer: No. Strike takes 'Link stands ready'; from behind the shield Link must lower it first.
duel-revised.maps.derived: Arcs: strike takes neutral; it is the only seat verb that gives striking.

duel-revised.maps.question: What does a successful block do in this draft?
duel-revised.maps.answer: It stops the blow, pushes Link back, and returns the enemy to idle. Link stays behind the shield.
duel-revised.maps.derived: Arcs: block takes attack, needs guarding, gives idle.

duel-revised.maps.question: Does Link ever have to decide while the enemy's blow is in the air?
duel-revised.maps.answer: No. The world resolves the blow (hit, block, or whiff) in the same exchange it swings, before Link speaks again.
duel-revised.maps.derived: probe.ts: no resting moment has attack marked. hit, block, and evade (priorities 12, 11, 10) outrank the beat (tick, 8) and the swing (6).

duel-revised.maps.question: How many resting moments are there?

duel-held.maps.question: When the enemy has wound up and a beat passes, how likely is it to swing at once?
duel-held.maps.answer: 3 in 5 (60%). Otherwise (40%) it holds the swing back for a beat.
duel-held.maps.derived: Arcs: swing (weight 3) and feint (weight 2) both take windup and ebeat at priority 6, a chance tie. probe.ts (neutral, windup) wait: 0.600 hit, 0.400 (neutral, delay).

duel-held.maps.question: While the enemy holds its swing back, what can Link do, and what happens?
duel-held.maps.answer: Hold: the late swing hits Link. Strike: the strike catches the held swing and Link lands a hit. Raise the shield: the late swing is blocked. Roll: the late swing whiffs and the enemy is left recovering.
duel-held.maps.derived: probe.ts moment (neutral, delay): wait > late, hit; strike > catch; guard > late, block; roll > late, evade.

duel-held.maps.question: During the wind-up, which choices are safe whatever the enemy does?
duel-held.maps.answer: Raising the shield and rolling. Holding or striking gets Link hit 60% of the time.
duel-held.maps.derived: probe.ts (neutral, windup): guard and roll lead to no outcome on either branch; wait and strike reach 'Link takes a hit' at 0.600.

duel-held.maps.question: Where are the punish windows?
duel-held.maps.answer: Two: while the enemy recovers after an evade, and while it holds the swing back.
duel-held.maps.derived: Arcs: punish takes recover and needs striking; catch takes delay and needs striking. probe.ts: strike at (neutral, recover) and (neutral, delay) gives enemy_hit.

duel-held.maps.question: Who decides whether the enemy feints?
duel-held.maps.answer: Nobody chooses. The world decides by chance, at 3 to 2 odds.
duel-held.maps.derived: swing and feint are world verbs tied at priority 6 with weights 3 and 2.

duel-held.maps.question: If Link rolls during the wind-up and the enemy holds the swing, what then?
duel-held.maps.answer: Link comes out of the roll standing ready while the enemy still holds the swing. Link chooses again, and a strike now lands.
duel-held.maps.derived: probe.ts (neutral, windup) roll: 0.400 tick > feint > rollend to (neutral, delay); (neutral, delay) strike > catch.

duel-held.maps.question: How many resting moments are there?

stamina-souls.maps.question: What does each of Link's actions cost in stamina?
stamina-souls.maps.answer: Strike costs 1, roll costs 2. Hold, raise the shield, and lower the shield are free.
stamina-souls.maps.derived: Arcs: strike takes stamina, roll takes 2 stamina; no other seat verb touches stamina.

stamina-souls.maps.question: When does stamina recover?
stamina-souls.maps.answer: Only when Link holds: each hold gives one breath, which becomes one stamina unless stamina is already full.
stamina-souls.maps.derived: Arcs: only wait gives breath; catch_breath takes breath, unless 3 stamina, gives stamina; breath_spent discards breath otherwise.

stamina-souls.maps.question: What is the most stamina Link can have?
stamina-souls.maps.answer: 3, which is also where Link starts.
stamina-souls.maps.derived: Arcs: stamina marks 3; catch_breath is blocked by unless 3 stamina and is the only verb that gives stamina. probe.ts: no moment holds more than 3.

stamina-souls.maps.question: How much stamina must Link have during the wind-up to roll under the swing and then punish?
stamina-souls.maps.answer: Full stamina, 3. The roll costs 2 and the strike costs 1, and nothing recovers in between.
stamina-souls.maps.derived: probe.ts: at (neutral, windup, stamina 3) roll leads to (neutral, recover, stamina 1), which offers strike > punish. At stamina 2, roll leads to (neutral, recover, stamina 0), which offers only wait and guard.

stamina-souls.maps.question: With 1 stamina during the wind-up, what keeps Link safe?
stamina-souls.maps.answer: Only raising the shield. Roll is not offered; holding or striking gets Link hit.
stamina-souls.maps.derived: probe.ts (neutral, windup, stamina 1): wait > hit; strike > hit; guard > block. roll needs 2 stamina.

stamina-souls.maps.question: Can Link recover stamina behind the shield?
stamina-souls.maps.answer: Yes, by holding behind it. Raising or lowering the shield recovers nothing.
stamina-souls.maps.derived: probe.ts (guarding, idle, stamina 1) wait > catch_breath to stamina 2. Arcs: guard and lower do not give breath.

stamina-souls.maps.question: How many resting moments are there?

stamina-hunter.maps.question: What does each of Link's actions cost in stamina?
stamina-hunter.maps.answer: Roll costs 2. Strike, hold, and the shield are free.
stamina-hunter.maps.derived: Arcs: roll takes 2 stamina; no other seat verb touches stamina.

stamina-hunter.maps.question: When does stamina recover?
stamina-hunter.maps.answer: Every beat, whatever Link does: one stamina per beat, up to the cap of 3.
stamina-hunter.maps.derived: Arcs: tick (a world verb every seat verb triggers through beat) gives breath; catch_breath takes breath unless 3 stamina.

stamina-hunter.maps.question: After rolling under a swing, can Link always punish?
stamina-hunter.maps.answer: Yes. Strikes are free, so every evade can be followed by a strike that lands.
stamina-hunter.maps.derived: probe.ts: every resting moment with recover and neutral marked offers strike > punish.

stamina-hunter.maps.question: How much stamina does Link need during the wind-up to dodge the swing?
stamina-hunter.maps.answer: 2. With 1 stamina, roll is not offered and only the shield keeps Link safe.
stamina-hunter.maps.derived: Arcs: roll takes 2 stamina. probe.ts (neutral, windup, stamina 1) offers wait, strike, guard; only guard avoids hit.

stamina-hunter.maps.question: From full stamina, how many rolls can Link make in a row?
stamina-hunter.maps.answer: Two. Each roll nets minus 1 after the beat's recovery: 3, then 2, then 1, and at 1 roll is not offered.
stamina-hunter.maps.derived: probe.ts: (neutral, idle, 3) roll > (neutral, windup, 2) roll > (neutral, recover, 1), which offers no roll.

stamina-hunter.maps.question: Who decides that stamina recovers?
stamina-hunter.maps.answer: The world, on every beat. Link cannot choose to recover or to skip it.
stamina-hunter.maps.derived: Arcs: the only giver of breath is tick, by world.

stamina-hunter.maps.question: How many resting moments are there?

stamina-third.maps.question: What does each of Link's actions cost in stamina?
stamina-third.maps.answer: Strike costs 1 and roll costs 1. Hold and the shield are free.
stamina-third.maps.derived: Arcs: strike takes stamina, roll takes stamina.

stamina-third.maps.question: When does stamina recover?
stamina-third.maps.answer: Only when a roll makes the enemy's blow whiff. A clean evade gives 2 breath, up to the cap of 3.
stamina-third.maps.derived: Arcs: only evade gives breath (2 breath); catch_breath takes breath unless 3 stamina.

stamina-third.maps.question: Can Link run out of stamina for good?
stamina-third.maps.answer: Yes. At 0 stamina Link cannot roll, so cannot evade, so never recovers. From then on the duel can only end with Link taking a hit, or go on forever behind the shield.
stamina-third.maps.derived: probe.ts: moments (neutral, windup), (guarding, idle), (guarding, windup) with no stamina can still reach only 'Link takes a hit'.

stamina-third.maps.question: What does a clean evade earn from 2 stamina?
stamina-third.maps.answer: Link ends with 3: the roll costs 1 and the evade restores 2.
stamina-third.maps.derived: probe.ts (neutral, windup, 2) roll > evade > catch_breath twice to (neutral, recover, 3).

stamina-third.maps.question: What does a strike into an idle enemy cost?
stamina-third.maps.answer: 1 stamina, never refunded, and the enemy simply winds up.

stamina-third.maps.question: Can Link punish after any evade?
stamina-third.maps.answer: Yes. An evade always leaves at least 2 stamina, and the strike costs 1.
stamina-third.maps.derived: probe.ts: every resting moment with recover and neutral marked has stamina 2 or 3 and offers strike > punish.

stamina-third.maps.question: How many resting moments are there?

call-the-coin.maps.question: Who speaks first?
call-the-coin.maps.answer: The world. It flips the coin before the caller can call.
call-the-coin.maps.derived: engine whoseTurn at the start: world, flip_heads and flip_tails at 0.5 each.

call-the-coin.maps.question: Can the caller see how the coin landed?
call-the-coin.maps.answer: No. Both covered states are hidden from every seat.
call-the-coin.maps.derived: heads and tails are seen-by none.

call-the-coin.maps.question: What are the caller's odds of winning, and does the call matter?
call-the-coin.maps.answer: Even, 1 in 2, whichever way the caller calls.
call-the-coin.maps.derived: flips are tied at weight 1; probe.ts: from each covered side, one call wins and one loses.

call-the-coin.maps.question: What does the caller hear when the coin lands?
call-the-coin.maps.answer: Only that the world acted, not which side.
call-the-coin.maps.derived: engine heardBy for caller: flip_heads and flip_tails heard as acted, because they touch hidden states.

call-the-coin.maps.question: Does whether the caller may call tell them anything about the coin?
call-the-coin.maps.answer: No. The calls depend only on 'Caller may call', never on the covered coin.
call-the-coin.maps.derived: Arcs: call_heads and call_tails take may_call only; check reports no leak warning.

call-the-coin.maps.question: How many distinct plays are there, and how do they end?
call-the-coin.maps.derived: engine.ts: plays 4, playsBy Caller wins 2, Caller loses 2.

tic-tac-toe.maps.question: After a mark, in what order does the world respond?
tic-tac-toe.maps.answer: First it checks for three in a row, then for a full board, then passes the turn.
tic-tac-toe.maps.derived: line verbs priority 2, board_full priority 1, pass_to_o and pass_to_x priority 0.

tic-tac-toe.maps.question: How does the game know the board is full?
tic-tac-toe.maps.answer: By absence: the draw rule fires only when no squares are left.
tic-tac-toe.maps.derived: board_full has unless squares_left; every mark takes squares_left, which starts at 9.

tic-tac-toe.maps.question: Can O's move ever end in a draw?
tic-tac-toe.maps.answer: No. Only X's move is judged for a full board, because X makes the ninth mark.
tic-tac-toe.maps.derived: board_full takes judge_x only; no draw verb takes judge_o.

tic-tac-toe.maps.question: How many complete games are there, and how do they end?
tic-tac-toe.maps.answer: 255,168: X wins 131,184, O wins 77,904, and 46,080 are drawn.

tic-tac-toe.maps.question: How many of X's winning lines use the center square?
tic-tac-toe.maps.derived: Arcs: four verbs need x_5 (x_line_456, x_line_258, x_line_159, x_line_357).

comparisons.question: What changed between the first and revised drafts?
comparisons.answer: Three things. Strike from guard is gone. The strike that breaks the wind-up is gone. A block now pushes Link back and returns the enemy to idle instead of making it reel into recovery.
comparisons.derived: Arc diff: duel-first has guard_strike and interrupt; block gives recover in duel-first and idle in duel-revised. Every other verb and arc is identical.

comparisons.question: What does the revision do to the punish windows?
comparisons.answer: The first draft has three ways to land a hit: strike during the wind-up, strike after a block, strike after an evade. The revision leaves one: strike after an evade.
comparisons.derived: probe.ts on both: moments where some choice reaches enemy_hit at odds 1. First: (neutral, windup), (guarding, windup), (neutral, recover), (guarding, recover). Revised: (neutral, recover) only.

comparisons.question: Which draft has a move that is always right during the wind-up, and what replaces it?
comparisons.answer: The first: striking during any wind-up wins outright, so the wind-up is no threat. In the revision the same strike gets Link hit; the answer to a wind-up becomes a roll, then a strike.
comparisons.derived: probe.ts (neutral, windup) strike: first > interrupt (Link lands a hit); revised > whiff, tick, swing, hit (Link takes a hit).

comparisons.question: Is the shield safer or more rewarding in one draft than the other?
comparisons.answer: Equally safe, less rewarding in the revision. Holding the shield blocks every swing in both, but only the first draft turns a block into a punish window.
comparisons.derived: block needs guarding in both. probe.ts: after a block, first reaches (guarding, recover) which offers guard_strike > punish; revised reaches (guarding, idle).

comparisons.question: How many resting moments does each draft have?
comparisons.answer: First 6, revised 5. The revision loses (guarding, recover), the enemy reeling while Link is behind the shield.
comparisons.derived: engine.ts positions minus outcomes; probe.ts moment lists.

comparisons.question: Where does recovery come from in each variant?
comparisons.answer: Souls: from holding still, Link's own choice. Hunter: from every beat, automatically. Third: from a clean evade, 2 at a time. The recovery machinery is the same in all three; only the verb that gives breath differs.
comparisons.derived: Arcs: give breath on wait (souls), tick (hunter), evade 2 (third). check-shared.ts: 'stamina recovery' subnet identical in all three.

comparisons.question: What does the dodge-then-punish combo cost in each, and when is it available?
comparisons.answer: Souls: 3 stamina, so only from full. Hunter: 2, and the punish itself is free. Third: 2, and the evade refunds 2, so it pays for itself.
comparisons.derived: Arcs: roll and strike take counts (souls 2+1, hunter 2+0, third 1+1); evade gives 2 breath in third. probe.ts ss4, sh3, st4.

comparisons.question: In which variant can Link end up with no way to win?
comparisons.answer: Only the third. At 0 stamina Link cannot roll, so cannot earn stamina back. In Souls holding refills, and in Hunter the beat refills.
comparisons.derived: probe.ts: every resting moment in souls and hunter can still reach both outcomes; third has three moments that reach only 'Link takes a hit'.

comparisons.question: Why does the third variant feel different from the Souls one?
comparisons.answer: Souls rewards patience: stepping back and holding refills stamina. The third rewards nerve: only reading the swing and rolling under it refills, so aggression pays for itself and wasted strikes are never refunded.
comparisons.derived: Arcs: souls wait gives breath; third evade gives 2 breath and wait gives nothing. probe.ts st5: a whiffed strike in third is a permanent loss.

comparisons.question: How many resting moments does each variant have?
